**Identify individuals.**

We have now completed the assembly of the dataset containing all individuals in the experiment (`ds_individuals`), each linked with morphological and behavioral traits. As we have recorded the mono-cultures of species just prior to the experiment, we can construct a support vector machine model capable of identifying a protist species based on its morphology and behavior. To establish this model, we must initially acquire the training dataset comprising monoculture data, which will serve as the basis for species identification modeling.

```{r}

# Import the master (aka particles) data where particles in each video have been tracked.  

training_individuals = get(load(here("data",
                                     "BEMOVI_output",
                                     paste0(threshold, "_threshold_analysis"),
                                     "training",
                                     merged_data_folder,
                                     "Master.RData"))) %>%
  
  # To get rid of particles that are not protists, filter the dataset according to particles that are too slow (filter_min_net_disp), don't move for enough time (filter_min_duration), are not detected for an enough number of frames (filter_detection_freq), and ... (filter_median_step_length). 

  filter_data(.,
              filter_min_net_disp,
              filter_min_duration,
              filter_detection_freq,
              filter_median_step_length) %>%
  
  # To increase the precision of the model, exclude Eug from the training monocultures, as we don't want species in heterotrophic to be mistaken for Euglena, as Euglena was not present in there. It doesn't matter how species in autotrophic ecosystems are identified, as we will change them anyway to Euglena. 

  filter(species != "Eug") %>%
  
  # To make it easier to handle the level, transform Spi te into Spi_te. 

  mutate(species = case_when(species == "Spi te " ~ "Spi_te",
                             TRUE ~ species)) %>%
  
  # To have each individual as a single row, link the same particle in different frames. 

  summarize_trajectories(.,
                         calculate.median = FALSE,
                         write = TRUE,
                         here("data", 
                              "BEMOVI_output", 
                              paste0(threshold, "_threshold_analysis"), 
                              "training", ""),
                         merged_data_folder) %>% 
  
  # To don't create rows with unnecessary NAs, remove the column "comment", as no entry received a comment in the experiment.
  
  mutate(comment = NULL,
         file = as.numeric(str_extract(file, "\\d+"))) %>%
  
  # To don't have particles where some values couldn't be computed, remove rows that have NAs.
  
  filter(complete.cases(.)) %>% 
  
  # To tidy up, reorder columns.
  
  select(file,
         id,
         species,
         N_frames,
         mean_area,
         everything())
```

Now that we have a training dataset with the morphological and behavioral traits of protists, we can construct a predictive model for species identification from such a dataset using support vector machines. We use for prediction all the traits we have measured.

```{r}
  species_ID_model = svm(
    factor(species) ~
      mean_grey +
      sd_grey +
      mean_area +
      sd_area +
      mean_perimeter +
      mean_turning +
      sd_turning +
      sd_perimeter +
      mean_major +
      sd_major +
      mean_minor +
      sd_minor +
      mean_ar +
      sd_ar +
      duration +
      max_net  +
      net_disp +
      net_speed +
      gross_disp +
      max_step +
      min_step +
      sd_step +
      sd_gross_speed +
      max_gross_speed +
      min_gross_speed ,
    data = training_individuals,
    probability = T,
    na.action = na.pass)
```

This model is not perfect and will make mistakes, which will be more or less common for different species. To see with what precision species are identified, let's plot the confusion matrix of this model. In this matrix, the so-called class error tells us with what percentage individuals of a species are misidentified.

```{r}
confusion_matrix = table(species_ID_model$fitted,
                         training_individuals$species)

confusion_matrix_with_diagonal_zeros = confusion_matrix
diag(confusion_matrix_with_diagonal_zeros) = 0

confusion_matrix = cbind(confusion_matrix,
                         class_error = rowSums(confusion_matrix_with_diagonal_zeros) / 
                                       rowSums(confusion_matrix)) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(class_error_percentage = class_error * 100,
         class_error = NULL) %>%
  print()
```

Now that we've examined the confusion matrix and confirmed the model's adequacy, let's proceed to determine the species classification for each protist individual in the dataset. Given that autotrophic ecosystems exclusively harbor the monoculture of *Euglena gracilis* (Eug), we can simply designate Eug as the species for each individual in autotrophic ecosystems.

```{r}

ds_individuals = ds_individuals %>%
  mutate(species = as.character(predict(object = species_ID_model,
                                        .,
                                        type = "response")),
         species = ifelse(trophic_type == "autotrophic",
                          "Eug",
                          species),
         
         # To make it easier to handle the level, transform Spi te into Spi_te. 

         species = case_when(species == "Spi te " ~ "Spi_te",
                             TRUE ~ species))
```
